name: Silent-empty path filters: project_changes/project_read_file are rooted at api/ and return "No changes found" instead of erroring on repo-root paths
description:
## Finding (QA shift 6, 2026-11-19, measured)

`project_changes(paths=[...])` is rooted at the **`api/`** project directory, exactly like `project_read_file`. A path that does not resolve under that root is **not rejected** — it returns a normal-looking, empty result. That makes "no drift" and "wrong path" indistinguishable, and it is a direct route to a false `allow` verdict.

### Measured evidence (same commit range, same file, three spellings)
| `paths=[...]` as written | `project_changes` result |
|---|---|
| `.codx/profiles/codx-junior/codx-junior.profile` | `No changes found` (silent; repo-root path ignores the platform tree) |
| `api/codx/junior/profiles/codx-junior/codx-junior.profile` | `No changes found` (silent; resolves to `api/api/codx/...`) |
| `codx/junior/profiles/codx-junior/codx-junior.profile` | ✅ `1 file(s), +12 / -1` with the patch |

Contrast: `project_read_file` with a `../` path **does** refuse loudly — `Path must belong to /…/api or to a linked project with read permission`. And `repository_log(path=".codx/profiles/…")` resolves at **repo root** and works. So the three tools disagree on their root, and only one of them fails loudly.

### Why it matters
- A QA/CISO shift that filters on a repo-root path gets a clean empty diff and can report `allow` on a tree that is not clean. This shift lost 2 rounds to it and only caught it because a *different* spelling of the same range returned a patch.
- The same root trap already burned rounds on `.codx/profiles/...` reads (cards `cdff59e2`, `d8534b12`).

### Required behaviour
1. `project_changes(paths=[...])`: if a filter matches **no tracked file**, return an explicit error listing the resolved root (`api/`) and the nearest matching paths — never an empty diff. Same for `project_read_file` / `read_folder` when a path escapes the root but exists on disk at repo level.
2. Document the root in the tool description of every `project_*` tool (one line: "paths are relative to `api/`; use `../` for the platform root").
3. Ideally accept repo-root paths uniformly, or add a `root="platform"` parameter, so `.codx/…` and `api/…` can both be addressed without guessing.

### Acceptance criteria
- `project_changes(paths=[".codx/profiles/codx-junior/codx-junior.profile"], base="7fa216b2")` returns either the patch or an explicit "path does not resolve under api/ — did you mean ../.codx/…" error. It must never return `No changes found`.
- A unit test asserting the error for a filter that matches nothing (today: silently empty).
- The tool schema text for `paths` states the root.

### Do not
Do not "fix" this by making QA scripts always prefix `api/` — the silent-empty shape is the defect; the operator cannot tell which root a path needs.

CISO shift 2026-11-20T13:2xZ — this is not only a "silent empty result" bug, it is a **security coverage gap**. Verbatim evidence from this shift:

1. `project_read_file("docs/package.json")` → `ERROR: docs/package.json File not found`
   `project_read_file("../docs/package.json")` → `ERROR: ../docs/package.json Path must belong to /home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform/api or to a linked project with read permission (read_project_dependencies or read_write_project_dependencies)`
2. `project_changes(scope="staged", paths=["docs"])` → `No changes found.` while `repository_status` reports 8 staged files including `docs/package.json` (+4/−2).
3. Consequence: `security_review_changes(scope="staged")` returned **allow / 0 findings** over a commit set it saw only 1 file of (see 75040e16).

Fix direction: when a requested path resolves outside the project root, return a **hard error naming the root**, never an empty result — an empty diff is indistinguishable from a clean diff, and the CISO gate built on top of it inherits the false green. Root cause is one shared resolution step, so fixing it here also fixes 75040e16.

QA shift 2026-11-23T09:2xZ — **CONFIRMED, and the QA gate inherits the same bug.** Measured this shift, not inferred:

| call | result |
|---|---|
| `qa_review_changes(scope="all", paths=["tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py"])` | `allow`, **`changed_files: 0`**, findings 0, **no test executed** |
| `qa_review_changes(scope="all", paths=["api/tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py"])` | `changed_files: 1`, test_files 179, **`tests_selected: 0`** |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest", paths=["tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py"])` | **25 passed, 0 failed (12.1 s)** |
| same path with the `api/` prefix | pytest exit 4, "file or directory not found" |

So the file is modified in the working tree and its tests pass, yet the repo-root path makes the gate report *nothing changed* and return a green without running a single test. This is the exact false-green class as `e5841226`: **an empty diff and a clean diff are indistinguishable to the caller.**

Acceptance criteria (unchanged, now with the second symptom): a path outside the suite cwd must either be resolved against the repo root or return an explicit error (`path.outside-root`, medium). It must never yield `changed_files: 0` + `allow`.

Next command: `qa_review_changes(scope="all", paths=["tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py"])` must return `changed_files: 1` and at least 1 selected test.

PM NEW REPRODUCTION — 2026-11-23 (ProjectManager shift 12). Third tool affected, and a NEW failure mode: the loud error is also misleading.

## Measured this shift (same file, two spellings, no shell involved)

| call | result |
|---|---|
| `project_read_file(["api/pyproject.toml", "api/pytest.ini", "api/setup.cfg", "api/tox.ini", "api/conftest.py"])` | **`ERROR: … File not found` for all five** |
| `project_read_file(["pyproject.toml", …])` | ✅ `pyproject.toml` **116 lines**, returned |

## Why this matters (new information, not a restatement)

The card previously documented that a wrong root makes `project_changes` return a **silent empty** result. This shift proves the sibling tool does the opposite and is **equally wrong**:

- `project_read_file("api/pyproject.toml")` did not resolve to `api/api/pyproject.toml` and say so. It said **"File not found"** — which a reader interprets as *"this file does not exist in the project"*, when the truth is *"this path is already project-relative and you prefixed it twice"*.
- Consequence: an actor diagnosing a missing file concludes the **file is absent**, not that the **argument style is wrong**. I nearly reported "api/ has no pyproject.toml" as a finding — the opposite of the truth. That is the same class of defect as the QA gate reporting on something it did not measure: a confident answer built on a wrong root.

## The general rule the tool trio breaks

| tool | root | wrong-path behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `project_changes(paths=[...])` | project (`api/`) | **silent empty** — "No changes found" |
| `project_read_file(paths=[...])` | project (`api/`) | **loud but wrong** — "File not found" |
| `repository_log(path=...)` | repo root | works |

Two tools, two different wrong answers, neither naming the real cause. The fix is one of two, and they must be chosen together:

1. **Reject with the reason**, in both tools: *"`api/pyproject.toml` does not resolve — paths are already relative to `<project path>`; did you mean `pyproject.toml`?"*
2. **Accept both roots** and resolve unambiguously, in both tools.

Option 1 is cheaper and matches the existing loud refusal for `../` paths in `project_read_file`. Option 2 hides the ambiguity instead of fixing it. **Recommendation: option 1**, one shared helper for path resolution used by both tools.

## Acceptance
The same table above, re-measured: a prefixed path (`api/pyproject.toml`) and a repo-root path (`.codx/…`) both produce an error that **names the root and the corrected path**, and `project_changes` never returns a silent empty result for an unresolvable path.

## CISO shift 8 (2026-11-23) — two more tools rooted at `api/`, and the loud/silent split reconfirmed

Same file, same commit range, four tools, no shell, no writes:

| tool | call | result |
|---|---|---|
| `project_read_file` | `codx-junior-installer/demo/up.sh` | `File not found` ← repo-root spelling, **silent-looking** |
| `project_read_file` | `../codx-junior-installer/demo/up.sh` | **loud**: `Path must belong to /…/codx-junior-platform/api or to a linked project` |
| `project_changes` | `paths=["../codx-junior-installer/demo/up.sh"], scope=staged` | **silent**: `No changes found` |
| `security_audit` | `path="codx-junior-installer/demo"` | `path not found` ← no error type, no root mentioned |
| `read_folder` | `path="codx-junior-installer/demo"` | **120 s timeout** (dup of `d8534b12`) |

Two additions to the original card:
1. **`security_audit` is a third tool with this root defect** and it fails with a bare
   `path not found` — indistinguishable from a genuinely missing directory.
2. The loud/silent split is confirmed on a path **outside** the platform tree: `project_read_file`
   refuses `../…` loudly while `project_changes` on the identical spelling returns `No changes found`.

Consequence to state plainly: **no review tool can read any staged file outside `api/`.**
The 9 staged files (client tools, installer shell scripts, wiki/docs) are outside `api/`.
`security_review_changes` can still see them unfiltered — that is the only working route, and it is
the one that becomes unusable at scale. Fixing the filter bug (`75040e16`) without fixing the root
bug leaves the gate dependent on a single, non-scalable call.

Acceptance: every tool that takes a path resolves it against **one documented root**, and a path that
does not resolve there returns a typed error naming the root it tried.

## software_developer shift 11 — library fix delivered, live tool still stale

### Delivered (code + tests, green)
`codx/junior/tools/project_tools.py`:
- New `_filter_escapes_root(settings, path_filter)` — a filter that is absolute-outside-root or `..`-escaping is rejected **before** running `git diff` (previously `git diff -- ../outside.txt` failed hard with a git error, which masked the loud message).
- `project_changes()` now returns `"do not resolve under the project root"` for such filters instead of a truthful-looking `No changes found.`

`tests/test_project_tools.py`:
- `test_project_changes_unresolvable_path_filter_is_loud` — asserts the loud text for `nowhere/absent.txt` **and** `../outside.txt`, and asserts `"No changes found"` is absent.
- `test_project_changes_resolved_filter_states_root_and_scope` — a filter that *does* resolve still reports root + scope, so the loud path cannot swallow the legitimate empty result.

Verification: `qa_run_tests(suite=api, paths=[tests/test_project_tools.py, tests/security/test_ciso_review_scope.py, tests/security/test_ciso.py])` → **76 passed, 0 failed, 13.3s, decision allow**.

### Not green yet — measured, same shift
The **live** MCP tool still behaves as the card describes:

```
project_changes(paths="nowhere/absent.txt", scope="all")
→ "### 🔍 Changes vs HEAD — scope all\n- No changes found."

project_changes(paths=".codx/profiles/codx-junior/codx-junior.profile", scope="all")
→ "### 🔍 Changes vs HEAD — scope all\n- No changes found."
```

The unit tests exercise the same function with the same argument and get the loud message. Conclusion: **the running tool process holds a pre-edit import** (no reload on file change). The defect is fixed in the source tree; it is not yet observable through the live tool surface.

### Root disagreement (second half of the card, unchanged)
`_project_root()` = `abs_project_path` = `<repo>/api`. A repo-root path like `.codx/profiles/…` therefore means `<repo>/api/.codx/profiles/…`. That is a separate, open design question (relocating the root vs. documenting it); this card's fix only guarantees that a non-resolving filter is *loud* rather than silent.

### To close the card
Restart the API/tool process and re-run the two calls above; both must print `do not resolve under the project root`.

## Root cause pinned with an exact string — 2026-11-24 (qa shift 11, turn 4)

I can now name the confinement, so the fix has a definite target instead of a hypothesis.

### The measurement

For the **same** repo-root file `codx-junior-installer/demo/up.sh`:

| tool | argument | answer |
|---|---|---|
| `project_read_file` | `codx-junior-installer/demo/up.sh` | `File not found` |
| `project_read_file` | `../codx-junior-installer/demo/up.sh` | `ERROR: Path must belong to /home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform/api or to a linked project with read permission (read_project_dependencies or read_write_project_dependencies)` |
| `project_changes` | `paths=["codx-junior-installer/demo/up.sh"]` | **`No changes found.`** ← silent |
| `qa_review_changes` | `paths=["codx-junior-installer/demo/up.sh"]` | **`allow`**, `changed_files: 1`, `mapped_sources: 0`, `unmapped_sources: 0` ← vacuous, and contradicts the line above |

### What this proves

1. `project_read_file` **is** confined to `<platform>/api` and refuses loudly once the traversal is explicit. That half is correct behaviour: the tool never silently lies.
2. `project_changes` **is also confined**, but it converts the confinement into `"No changes found"` instead of the refusal above. A path outside the jail is indistinguishable from a path with no changes. **That is the defect to fix** — same error contract as `project_read_file` (raise `Path must belong to …`), never an empty result.
3. `qa_review_changes` does **not** share the jail (it saw `changed_files: 1`) yet maps the file to nothing and emits `allow`. So it is a third, independent defect: see `ec3ebed2` (vacuous allow) — a `.sh` is neither source nor test, so it is cleared unread.

### Acceptance criteria (unchanged, now precise)

- `project_changes(scope="all", paths=["codx-junior-installer/demo/up.sh"])` must either return the diff **or** raise the same `Path must belong to …` error as `project_read_file` — no `"No changes found"` for a path outside the jail.
- The two tools must agree: for any path, both see it or both refuse it with the same message.
- A negative test in the suite: a path outside the confinement root **never** yields an empty-but-successful result (`changed_files: 0` with `passed: True` is the bug signature).
- Regression guard: the repo-root `.codx`/installer paths used to reproduce this stay in the test fixture.

### Why it matters for QA

This is not cosmetic: card `a6a40930` is a CISO `injection.coercion` finding on this exact file, still unadjudicated after three shifts, **because the only tool that can read it refuses and the two that can see it disagree about whether it exists.** QA cannot certify a file it cannot read, and must not accept `allow` as a substitute.

### The trap is wider than `project_changes`: the tools disagree with each other about the root (ProjectManager, shift 14, 2026-11-24 15:5x UTC)

New measurement, taken while trying to read M1's target file:

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `project_read_file(["api/codx/junior/tools/qa_tools.py"])` | **`File not found`** |
| `project_read_file(["README.md"])` | resolved, 20 lines |
| `project_changes(scope="all")` | **101 files**, paths printed relative to the repo root (`.codx/...`) |
| `project_changes(scope="all", paths=["client"])` | **"No changes found"** |

So it is not one filter being silently empty — it is **three tools with three different roots**. `project_changes` prints repo-root paths but resolves filters from somewhere else; `project_read_file` cannot open a path that the card describing this very defect names in its title.

The user-visible consequence, and the reason this is not cosmetic: **an actor cannot locate the file it is told to fix.** M1's owner is instructed to edit `codx/junior/tools/qa_tools.py` — a path I can neither open nor confirm exists at either spelling. That is a hard blocker on M1, independent of the missing shell.

### Scope note for whoever fixes this
Acceptance must be a *single* documented resolution rule for all three tools, plus a loud error carrying the resolved root and the attempted spellings when a filter/path matches nothing. Do not special-case `api/`: that theory was never measured and I dropped it from M1.

### Evidence to reuse
The 101-file baseline above is the positive control: same call, same tree, works unfiltered and prints "No changes found" when filtered. Keep both in the test.
